newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine employment up 3.2 percent in 12 months.
newsitem.headline: Argentine employment up 3.2 percent in 12 months.

text.p: Argentina's employment index grew almost one percent in February, bringing its 12-month rise to 3.2 percent, the Labor Ministry said Monday.
"This trend confirms the steady increase in annualized growth, which was 1.6 percent and 2.0 percent in December and January, respectively," the ministry said in a report.
The number of hours worked rose 3.3 percent in February to 223.5, including 35 hours of overtime.
The government expects gross domestic product to grow six percent this year and unemployment to drop to between 12 to 15 percent from the current 17.3 percent.
Financial and business sectors showed the biggest employment growth in February, gaining two percent from January, while construction jobs fell 1.4 percent.
Companies with between 50 and 199 employees registered the strongest job growth at two percent.
The report said 79.1 percent of new jobs were created through flexible labor contracts, while 48.5 percent of workers who left their jobs had indefinite contracts.
"The trend towards replacing workers hired for indefinite periods with personnel with more flexible hiring conditions is growing," it said.

Jobs growth is one indication of the trend in unemployment, a statistic that also depends on the size of the population actively seeking work. In recent years the number of job seekers has grown strongly and is blamed by the government for a surge in unemployment from seven percent in 1989, when President Carlos Menem took office.

According to government data, if the number of active job seekers had remained at 1990 levels, unemployment would have risen to just 11.2 percent in 1995 rather than the record 18.4 percent reached that month.
Private surveys have shown unemployment is the biggest concern of Argentines and their main complaint against the free market policies of the Menem administration.
